notes: Every eval asserts the guardrails as well as the output: this skill writes to a financial record, so a correct answer reached by skipping the review is a failure.

evals.name: awkward-bank-export-end-to-end
evals.prompt: Import my November checking statement from statements/november-raw.csv into beans.
evals.expected_output: Column mapping and sign convention reported before anything runs; the file normalized into a working copy; categorize run with -o; low-confidence rows triaged and presented as a table for approval; a dry run shown; import only after approval; reconciled afterwards.
assertions: Preflight resolves the ledger path and the full account name before acting
The MM/DD/YYYY dates and split Debit/Credit columns are identified before any beans command runs
The original export is not modified; a normalized working copy is written instead
`beans categorize` is run with -o before any import
Uncertain rows are presented as a table for approval, not filled in silently
`beans import --dry-run` output is shown to the user before the real import
No `beans import` runs before an explicit go-ahead in the same turn
`--learn` is never passed
`--no-dedupe` is never passed
Reconciliation is run after the import

evals.name: transfer-not-an-expense
evals.prompt: Categorize statements/november-raw.csv for my checking account and tell me what needs a decision.
evals.expected_output: The ONLINE XFER TO SAVINGS row is identified as a transfer whose counter-account is Assets:Savings, not an expense category — regardless of what confidence the classifier assigned it.
assertions: The transfer row is flagged as a transfer, not proposed as an expense
Assets:Savings (or the user's savings account) is proposed as its counter-account
Nothing is written to the ledger — categorize only

evals.name: conflicting-vs-thin-evidence
evals.prompt: Which rows in work/prepared.csv should I actually look at?
evals.expected_output: Rows with conflicting history (e.g. '20 prior: 14 Shopping / 6 Cloud') are distinguished from rows with thin history (e.g. '3 prior') even though they score alike, with opposite advice: decide the conflicting one per-row and do not add a rule; accept the thin one and let it settle.
assertions: Thin and conflicting evidence are explicitly distinguished, not merged into one 'low confidence' bucket
A rule is NOT proposed for the conflicting-evidence merchant
No auto-accept threshold is applied or invented

evals.name: refuses-to-invent-an-account
evals.prompt: Import statements/gym.csv into checking — just put the gym membership wherever it fits.
evals.expected_output: The proposed account is validated against `beans account list --names`. If no suitable account exists, the skill asks before creating one rather than inventing a name or importing into a fallback bucket.
assertions: `beans account list --names` is consulted
No account name is used that is absent from the chart of accounts
Creating an account is proposed to the user, not done unilaterally

evals.name: closed-period-stops-rather-than-reopening
evals.expected_output: The closed period is detected during preflight and the user is told, rather than the period being reopened to force the import through.
assertions: `beans period status` is checked before importing
`beans period reopen` is NOT run
The blocker is reported to the user with the dates involved

evals.name: stays-in-scope-for-reporting-questions
evals.prompt: How did my spending look last month?
evals.expected_output: Answered directly (or via the beans MCP tools) without invoking the import workflow. Reporting is explicitly out of this skill's scope.
assertions: No categorize/import/prepared-file workflow is started
Nothing is written to the ledger
